name: Multiplication (fundamental counting) principle
function_signature: (stages s_1,...,s_k with n_1,...,n_k choices each) → (total number of outcomes n_1·n_2·…·n_k)
description: The number of ways to perform a sequence of independent choices equals the product of the number of options available at each stage.

name: Ordered samples with replacement
description: The set of ordered r-tuples drawn with repetition allowed from n distinct objects, of which there are exactly n^r.

name: Ordered samples without replacement (permutations of r from n)
description: The set of ordered r-tuples of distinct elements chosen from n objects, of which there are exactly the falling factorial (n)_r = n!/(n−r)!.

name: Combinations with repetition (stars and bars)
function_signature: (n cell types, r indistinguishable items) → (number of unordered selections C(n+r−1, r))
description: A bijective counting technique placing r identical items into n categories by arranging r stars and n−1 bars, giving C(n+r−1, r) multisets.

name: Occupancy (balls in cells) model
description: The combinatorial probability model in which r balls are distributed among n cells, parametrizing classical distinguishability and exclusion assumptions.

name: Maxwell–Boltzmann statistics
description: The occupancy scheme in which r distinguishable balls are placed independently and uniformly into n cells, yielding n^r equally likely arrangements.

name: Boole's inequality (subadditivity)
description: The probability of a finite or countable union of events is at most the sum of their individual probabilities.

name: Multinomial theorem
description: The expansion of (x_1+…+x_m)^n as a sum over compositions of n of multinomial-coefficient-weighted monomials.

name: Probability of realizing exactly m of N events
description: The inclusion-exclusion-type formula expressing P(exactly m of N events occur) as an alternating sum of the binomial-weighted symmetric sums S_m, S_{m+1}, ….

name: Returns to the origin (u_{2n})
description: The probability u_{2n} that a simple symmetric random walk is back at the origin after 2n steps, equal to C(2n,n)2^{-2n}.

name: Iterated generating functions for branching processes
description: The generating function of the n-th generation size in a Galton–Watson process is the n-fold functional composition of the offspring generating function.

name: Sparre Andersen fluctuation theorem
description: A distribution-free combinatorial identity stating that for exchangeable increments the law of the number of positive partial sums equals the law of the index of the first maximum, underpinning random-walk fluctuation theory.

name: Independent increments process
description: A stochastic process whose increments over disjoint time intervals are mutually independent random variables.

name: Stationary increments
description: A stochastic process for which the distribution of an increment X_{t+h}−X_t depends only on the length h and not on the time t.

name: Bessel function densities
description: Probability densities expressed through modified Bessel functions, arising e.g. as first-passage densities of random walks and as laws of sums of independent exponential or noncentral chi-square variables.

name: Kolmogorov canonical representation
description: The canonical representation of the characteristic function of an infinitely divisible law with finite variance via a drift and a finite spectral measure K(dx), the finite-second-moment specialization of the Lévy–Khinchine formula.

name: Index of stability α
description: The exponent α ∈ (0,2] characterizing a stable distribution through the scaling relation of sums of i.i.d. copies and governing its tail behavior.

name: Types of distributions (affine equivalence)
description: The equivalence classes of distribution functions under affine transformations X ↦ aX+b (a>0), within which location and scale vary but shape is fixed.

name: Duality lemma for random walks
function_signature: (partial sums S_1,...,S_n of i.i.d. increments) → (equality in law with the reversed-order partial sums)
description: The time-reversal identity that the partial sums (S_1,…,S_n) have the same joint law as the reversed walk, relating first-passage and ladder events to maxima.
